name: obsidian-second-brain
cost: Free (MIT). Some research commands use paid APIs, at a few cents per call
works_with: Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Antigravity, Pi, Hermes and Grok Bot
short: Runs your Obsidian vault as a second brain: it saves notes from chats, rewrites pages from new sources and tidies itself on a schedule.
what: It gives your agent 49 commands for an Obsidian vault. `/obsidian-save` pulls the decisions, people, tasks and ideas out of a conversation and files each one in the right note. `/obsidian-ingest` takes a voice memo, photo, document or video link and updates your existing pages instead of adding one more summary. There are also research commands, a vault health check and Crew, a shared logbook so several agents know what the others did.
who: Obsidian users who already work with a coding agent and want their notes kept up to date for them. If you don't keep a vault, you can still use Crew on its own, but most of the pack won't matter to you.
needs: An Obsidian vault, or let it create one
A supported agent, such as Claude Code
Python 3.10 or newer and `uv` for the scripts
Optional: xAI Grok, Perplexity, Google Gemini, YouTube Data or OpenAI Whisper keys for some research commands

steps.title: Install the plugin in Claude Code
Tell it where your vault is
steps.text: Add this to the `env` section of `~/.claude/settings.json`.

steps.title: Set up the vault
steps.text: Restart Claude Code, then run this inside your vault. Plugin commands all start with `/obsidian-second-brain:`.

steps.title: Or install with the script
steps.text: Use this if you want bare command names like `/obsidian-init`.

steps.title: No vault yet?
steps.text: This creates one with folders, templates and boards.
steps.code:
cd ~/.claude/skills/obsidian-second-brain
uv run python scripts/bootstrap_vault.py --path ~/Documents/MyVault --name "Your Name"
bash scripts/setup.sh ~/Documents/MyVault

try.label: From the README
try.text: After a meeting, run `/obsidian-save`. Before a big decision, run `/obsidian-challenge` to have it search your vault for past failures and reversed decisions on the same topic.

watch: The README also offers a one-line install that pipes a script from GitHub straight into bash. Read the script first if you use it.

The optional background agent runs headless with `--dangerously-skip-permissions`. It ships off, is limited to read, write and edit tools with no shell or network, and only adds and updates notes. Leave it off if you don't want that.
Paid research calls have no hard caps. The README gives rough costs such as about $0.40 to $0.80 for `/research-deep`, and logs spend to `~/.research-toolkit/usage.log`.
It rewrites existing pages from new sources. The README says it never deletes or changes notes destructively without asking, but back up your vault first.
The calendar command needs the Google Calendar MCP connector.
